component.name: Copper
component.summary: A quiet WebKit browser with an agent built in

description.p: Copper is a small, fast browser on WebKit: one field, tabs in a column or a row, and the page. The Linux build is native Rust on GTK 4, libadwaita and WebKitGTK.

ul.li: Spaces, pinned tabs and private tabs
A built-in ad blocker, hide-anything and reading mode
History, bookmarks, downloads and passwords in the system keyring
Copper Cloud sync with Copper on the Mac
A local MCP server so coding agents can drive a tab

description.p: Calendar peek on the Google Calendar pin, folder-aware dragging, and pins that sync once per site.

ul.li: Rest on a Google Calendar pin to see your next meetings, with Join for video calls (Settings › Tabs › Calendar).
Dragging a row shows no marker over its own place, and can pin it even with no favourites yet.
Pins sync once per site across devices; a pin another device re-keys keeps its page.

description.p: Sign in to Copper Cloud with your company account from Settings, and open copper://cloud/join links there.

ul.li: Settings › Cloud signs in with your company account in the system browser (Continue with Google), for a sign-in link or an instance that offers it.
A copper://cloud/join link opens Settings › Cloud with the code, from the command line, a running Copper or the address field, and never switches to another instance without asking.
An instance with a publicly trusted certificate is no longer described as plain HTTP.

description.p: The Agent sidebar, filled by an addon from your Copper Cloud.

ul.li: Ctrl+E opens the Agent sidebar on the right of the window; drag its edge to change its width.
Copper Cloud decides which addon fills it. A new addon or version is checked and staged, Settings › Updates says Update available, and Install loads it without a relaunch.
Settings › Addons lists installed addons, turns one off on this computer, removes one, and checks for updates.

description.p: Sign in to Copper Cloud with your company account, and run Copper with no display as an agent's own browser.

ul.li: copper cloud sso signs in with your company account in the system browser; copper cloud pair pairs a profile while Copper is not running; copper cloud status shows the link, the account and the sync switches.
Copper Cloud sign-in links and copper://cloud/join deep links are recognised, and Copper registers itself for copper:// links.
A Copper Cloud code without a certificate fingerprint is checked against the public certificate authorities.
COPPER_ROUTER_URL and COPPER_ROUTER_KEY name the model router for a headless Copper.

description.p: Big canvases are fast, agents can read them a page at a time, and tabs are easier to keep.

ul.li: A canvas draws only what is on screen. Live web frames load only when they are on screen and big enough to read, a few at a time. A frame that is let go shows a snapshot of its site. Images drawn small use a small copy, and notes far zoomed out draw as simple blocks.

Agents read a big canvas in pages: canvas_read takes overview, frame, region, ids, types, query, limit and cursor. Canvas tools now wait for a canvas tab that is asleep, just restored or slow to load.
Ctrl+T lists Open Tabs, then History, then Search. Tab and Shift+Tab jump between the sections.
Closing a Saved tab keeps it in Saved, as in Arc. Only the row's close button removes it. You can drag a tab into Saved.

description.p: Installer refreshes apt package lists on fresh machines (fixes installs on clean Ubuntu and Debian).
